title: GreenGateway MCP Client Configuration Templates
description: What a running gateway serves at GET /v1{ADMIN_PREFIX}/mcp/client-configs (admin:mcp:clients:read) and what ggctl mcp-config reads: credential-free configuration templates for MCP clients, all naming the gateway's own MCP endpoint, which the gateway computes from GATEWAY_PUBLIC_URL as its protected-resource metadata does. An OAuth template holds only that URL; a token template names the fixed environment variable GREENGATEWAY_MCP_TOKEN in the client's interpolation syntax and never a token. The document is closed: a member this version does not define, a duplicate member, or a value outside its grammar makes it unreadable. This schema is necessary but not sufficient: the shared reader in the gateway-config crate is authoritative, and accepts a document only when every template is exactly what this version renders for the stated mcpUrl, serverName and oauth.

apiVersion.description: Exact document version. No other version, prefix, or spelling is accepted.

mcpUrl.description: The gateway's MCP endpoint in canonical URL form: https (http only for a loopback host), a path ending at /mcp, an optional query, no user information or fragment, and none of the characters $ { } \ that client configuration files interpolate or escape.

serverName.description: The server entry name the JSON templates use.

oauth.description: Whether the gateway's protected-resource metadata advertises an authorization server. OAuth templates are present only when it does.

tokenVariable.description: The environment variable every token template reads the bearer token from.

templates.description: For each client in the order generic, claude-desktop, cursor, vscode: its OAuth template when oauth is true, then its token template when it has one. Claude Desktop has no token template.

auth.description: oauth: the client discovers the authorization server from the gateway's protected-resource metadata. token: the client sends the bearer token it reads from tokenVariable.

format.description: json: a JSON document, the client's configuration file. url: one line holding the MCP URL, for a client that takes it in its own interface.

locations.description: Where the client reads a file holding this template, relative to a project or the user's home directory; empty for a client that takes the template in its own interface.

content.description: The template, ending in a line feed.
